$doc: Player movement, health, interaction and noise. Units: metres, seconds, radians.

movement.$note: Movement is speed-uniform in every direction on purpose - walking backwards while watching the enemy carries no penalty.

camera.$note: `fovDegrees` and `invertY` are the DEFAULTS the options menu starts from; `fovRange` is how far its slider may be dragged. `mouseSensitivity` is radians per pixel - the options slider scales it (input.json -> mouse.sensitivity), it does not replace it.

health.$giveUp: Nobody bleeds out, so the only way off the floor other than a teammate is to choose it. Long enough that it cannot be an accident, short enough that it is not a punishment for having decided.

noise.$doc: Emitted noise events. `radius` is the metre radius at which the enemy can perceive it (see enemy.json hearing). A loudness of 0 is genuinely silent - never heard, and no ring on the roster HUD.
noise.$note: `injured` is currently unused: injury costs speed, not stealth, so an injured player emits the same walk/sprint/crouch noise as a healthy one.
noise.$items: Thrown items are the only noise you get to AIM. `throwImpact` is anything landing; `alarm` is the clock re-emitting for as long as it rings; `blast` is the flashbang, which is loud enough to bring the hunter running if it was standing outside the blind radius; `wreck` is a player tearing a barricade off a door, which is exactly as quiet as it sounds.

customisation.$doc: What the wardrobe in the lobby offers. Colours are free and always available; hats are bought with the coins a run banks. Adding a hat is an entry in `hats` plus a builder registered as that `artId` in art/shared/characters/hats.ts - nothing else in the game has to change.
customisation.$hats: `cost` is in banked coins and 0 means it is yours from the start. `artId` must resolve in the shared art registry; an unknown one falls back to a bare head rather than failing a run. Order here is the order the wardrobe lists them in, so it doubles as the price ladder.

effects.$doc: Screen feedback. Distances in metres, measured enemy -> local player.
